types.name: ecuio_frame_t
types.decl:
typedef struct ecuio_frame {
    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* Microseconds since the session's transport
                                 attached, monotonic per channel. Mock: the
                                 host's steady clock. J2534: the host's at the
                                 first frame, then the adapter's own deltas,
                                 carried across its 32-bit wrap */
    uint32_t arbitration_id;  /* CAN identifier: <= 0x7FF standard, up to
                                 0x1FFFFFFF when FLAG_EXTENDED set */
    uint16_t channel_id;      /* Bus/channel index only — never multiplexes
                                 an arbitration ID */
    uint16_t data_length;     /* Bytes used in data[]: 0..64 */
    uint8_t  data[64];        /* Classic CAN (8) .. CAN-FD (64) payload */
    uint32_t flags;           /* ECUIO_FRAME_FLAG_* bitmask */
    uint32_t reserved;        /* Producers MUST leave zero; ABI growth space */
} ecuio_frame_t;
types.doc: Frame structure — POD only, no pointers. Layout is pinned by the assertions below: 88 bytes, no hidden padding on any supported platform (ADR-0006).

types.doc: POD, 432 bytes, no hidden padding on any supported platform; pinned by the assertions below. New fields take the reserved room.

types.name: ecuio_transport_ops_t
types.doc: Transport abstraction (internal): sessions own a transport instance polymorphically. ops is a pointer to static, immutable vtable storage owned by the transport implementation TU; impl is the implementation's private state. Both start() and detach() are invoked by the session, never by transports themselves — no re-entry into session lifecycle. Contract: - start(): called from ecuio_session_start. Must be idempotent (second call on a running transport returns ECUIO_OK). - detach(): called exactly once from ecuio_session_close, AFTER the closed flag is set. Must stop any worker threads and free impl + the ecuio_transport wrapper itself. May not touch session afterwards.

types.decl:
typedef struct ecuio_j2534_device {
    uint32_t vendor_id;           /* Index in discovery order (0-based) */
    char vendor_name[ECUIO_J2534_VENDOR_NAME_LEN];   /* registry key name */
    char dll_path[ECUIO_J2534_DLL_PATH_LEN];         /* FUNCTIONLIBRARY,
                                                        expanded; a path
                                                        too long for this
                                                        isn't listed */
    uint32_t supported_protocols; /* 0 — reserved for PROTOCOLS bitmask parse */
    uint32_t reserved[8];         /* ABI-stable expansion room
                                   * [0]: architecture (1=x86, 2=x64, 0=unknown) */
} ecuio_j2534_device_t;
types.doc: Text is UTF-8 throughout: vendor_name, dll_path, and the path forms of a j2534:// URI. Core passes paths to Windows as UTF-16.

types.name: ecuio_signal_def_t
types.doc: One signal, in three blocks: which frames carry it, how its bytes become a value, and how the value is shown. Every byte is a named field, so the compiler adds no padding. Reserved bytes and flags must be zero, so a later field can take that room and existing sets still load (ADR-0016). kind and byte_order are fixed-width fields because an enum's size is up to the compiler.

types.name: ecuio_channel_decl_t
ecuio_signal_set_t
types.doc: Fill a set member by member from a zeroed struct, never positionally: reserved0 sits between channel_count and channels.

types.name: ecuio_validation_t
types.doc: Why a set failed validation, and where. index names the element the code is about: the failing def; for a duplicate id, the second def of the pair; for a bad channel id, the channel; for a duplicate rx, the second channel of the pair. It is UINT32_MAX for ECUIO_VALIDATE_OK and for a code that names no single element: a NULL, the layout version, the set's reserved fields, the channel count.

types.name: ecuio_pid_scheduler
types.doc: Round-robin PID scheduler (ADR-0013). Fixed capacity, no allocation, owned exclusively by the transport worker thread — single-threaded by construction, so no synchronization inside. PID derivation rule (ecuio_mode01_pid): a def drives scheduling iff its mux key is the 2-byte [41][PID] echo at payload offset 0, which opens a Mode-01 response once the transport strips the address header. The PID to request is the key's low byte. Sets without such defs (raw, mock) enroll nothing, and the worker falls back to ?poll= or passive receive. Registration validates each def but not this shape (other mux keys are legal), so from_set() checks it itself.

types.doc: Negative-array-size idiom — valid in ALL C standards including pedantic C89, complementing the header's _Static_assert (C11+).
